# The status-check contexts REQUIRED to merge into `main`.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Branch protection lives on the server, so "is this check blocking?" was
# unanswerable from a clone -- and five places in this repo answered it differently: docs/CI.md
# listed 8 contexts, .github/workflows/manifest-lint.yml said 4, docs/design/freethread.md said 7,
# tests/test_push_guard.py said 12. With `required_approving_review_count: 0` and auto-merge armed,
# required-set membership is the ONLY thing separating "reviewed" from "merged unread", so a wrong
# answer here mis-ranks which gates a change can safely touch.
#
# It stopped being hypothetical within hours of this file landing. On 2026-07-29 branch protection was
# briefly reduced to a SINGLE required context -- the backlog-hygiene check -- dropping all twelve
# gates, every test leg and security scanner among them, while auto-merge stayed armed and approvals
# stayed at 0. Several PRs merged in that window. What surfaced it was reconciling a CI wait against
# `required_status_checks.contexts` and seeing the count come back as 1: a monitor that had waited for
# "nothing pending" would have reported green without ever waiting for a test leg, because with one
# required context there was nothing to wait for. Count what SHOULD gate the merge, not what does.
#
# The set then moved four more times the same day (1 -> 13 -> 12 -> 15 -> 12), and it moved again on
# 2026-08-31: `a reviewer has read this` was armed, and the two CodeQL matrix contexts were seen
# required earlier that day and are no longer. It moved once more on 2026-09-04, when the owner
# RETIRED the review requirement: `a reviewer has read this` was removed from protection, fourteen
# back to thirteen. It moved AGAIN between 2026-09-13 22:41Z and 2026-09-14 06:59Z, when the owner
# added the two `security.yml` composite roll-ups, thirteen to fifteen -- step 2 of the consolidation
# staged below. It moved ONCE MORE at about 2026-09-16 18:45Z, when the owner removed the SEVEN
# original `security.yml` scan contexts, fifteen back to EIGHT. That is consolidation step 4, taken
# BEFORE step 3 rather than after it -- the inversion the step-ordering note further down this file
# asked for, and the safe direction of the pair: removing a context can wedge nothing, while deleting
# a job protection still names wedges every pull request in the repository.
#
# THE LIST BELOW IS SET-EQUAL TO THE SERVER -- EIGHT contexts, nothing extra on either side --
# read at 2026-09-17 00:23Z with
# `gh api repos/MEFORORG/MessageFoundry/branches/main/protection --jq '.required_status_checks.contexts[]'`,
# by diffing the sorted API read against the sorted parse of this file.
# A set-equal read is the only one worth writing down: a count alone cannot tell a matching set from
# two offsetting errors.
#
# THE 2026-09-16 MOVE WENT UNMIRRORED TOO, AND FOR ABOUT SIX HOURS THIS FILE OVERSTATED THE GATE. It
# named fifteen over a server holding eight, so it asserted that seven security contexts block a merge
# when nothing required them. That is the OPPOSITE error from the one below -- over-claiming rather
# than under-claiming -- and it is the less dangerous of the two, because a reader who believes a gate
# is blocking treats the change as more constrained than it is. It is still a false answer to the one
# question this file exists to answer, and the seven were not idle: they still RUN on every pull
# request and still go red on a finding, so "is this check blocking?" and "does this check report?"
# came apart for the first time here. That distinction is why the seven are recorded below as
# superseded rather than deleted outright.
#
# THE 2026-09-14 MOVE IS THE ONE THIS FILE FAILED TO MIRROR IN THE REASSURING DIRECTION, AND IT IS
# RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN QUIETLY
# FIXED. For roughly a day the file named thirteen over a server holding fifteen, and the two it
# omitted were the two it explicitly described as "DELIBERATELY ABSENT ... a red one BLOCKS NOTHING
# TODAY". So the file did not merely lag -- it asserted the opposite of the server, in the reassuring
# direction, on the one question it exists to answer from a clone. A session counting passing checks
# against this file would have read a pull request as fully green with two required contexts still
# unreported. `scripts/ci/check_required_contexts_drift.py` DID detect it and reported to nobody.
# THAT IS AN ALERTING GAP, NOT A MISSING DETECTOR, and the difference matters because a reader who
# concludes the checker is unwired goes on to build a second one. It IS wired:
# `.github/workflows/required-workflow-state.yml`'s `accurate` job runs it on a 07:00 UTC cron, on
# `workflow_dispatch`, and on any pull request touching `.github/required-contexts.txt` or
# `.github/workflows/**`. That job is deliberately NOT a required context -- it reads the server, so
# requiring it would put every merge behind an API call -- and nothing watches its scheduled runs:
# `failure-signal.yml` watches CI, Security and backlog-hygiene only. So the cron goes red on the
# morning after a protection change and no pull request, label or notice carries it.
# `tests/test_required_contexts_drift.py` pins the wiring so the job cannot be deleted silently;
# giving its red a consumer is an alerting design over shared CI, still not done.
#
# Two non-context settings also change merge semantics and are described here. They are NOT recorded
# the same way, and the asymmetry is deliberate: `strict` carries a value, `enforce_admins` does not.
#
#   strict = TRUE  -- a PR must be up to date with `main` before it can merge. This closes the
#                     stale-green hole: previously a PR validated against an older base could merge
#                     without revalidation, so a semantic conflict with a newer `main` (a test that
#                     reads a file the other PR changed) could land red on main. Re-read 2026-09-04
#                     19:05 CDT.
#   enforce_admins -- WHEN ON, an admin's direct push to `main` is refused by the server and not
#                     merely by the local hook; WHEN OFF, the hook is the only thing refusing it.
#                     THE VALUE IS DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN DOWN, HERE OR ANYWHERE IT CAN BE HELPED.
#                     Read it:
#
#                         gh api repos/MEFORORG/MessageFoundry/branches/main/protection/enforce_admins
#
#                     THAT ENDPOINT IS ADMIN-ONLY AND ITS REFUSAL LOOKS LIKE AN ANSWER. Reading branch
#                     protection needs admin on the repository; GitHub answers a protection endpoint it
#                     will not show you with 404, not 403, which reads as "there is no protection here"
#                     rather than "you may not look". That is the dangerous direction -- it suggests a
#                     direct push to `main` would be accepted. Treat anything that is not a JSON body
#                     as NOT MEASURED. The same command is the pointer in scripts/hooks/push_guard.py,
#                     tests/test_push_guard.py, scripts/coord/install-git-hooks.ps1 and
#                     .github/workflows/branch-leak-scan.yml; the caveat is stated once, here.
#
#                     WHY NO COPY. Nothing in this repository reconciles this
#                     setting against the server -- `scripts/ci/check_required_contexts_drift.py`
#                     compares the CONTEXT SET and says so in its own docstring -- and it has moved
#                     repeatedly: ON 2026-07-28, OFF 2026-07-29 through the escape hatch in
#                     scripts/hooks/push_guard.py (for when a permanently red required check blocks
#                     every merge), read back TRUE 2026-08-31. Every in-repo copy went stale at least
#                     once, and they went stale in BOTH directions over their life. Over-stating
#                     protection invites `--no-verify` on the belief that something downstream still
#                     catches the push; under-stating it is a false statement delivered at the moment
#                     of action. Neither direction is safe, which is the argument against keeping a
#                     copy rather than for correcting one again.
#
#                     THE SAME ARGUMENT REACHES `strict`, AND IT IS NOT APPLIED THERE. That setting is
#                     no better reconciled -- the drift script's docstring excludes it by name too --
#                     and docs/CI.md carries a second copy of it. Its value above is a DATED READING,
#                     not a claim about now; read it from the same endpoint before relying on it. The
#                     asymmetry is history, not principle: `enforce_admins` was measured stale and
#                     repaired, `strict` has not been.
#
#                     WHAT THIS BLOCK USED TO SAY, because the shape recurs and the replacement is
#                     the point. It read "THREE OTHER PLACES STILL CARRY THE OFF VALUE AND ARE STALE"
#                     and named tests/test_push_guard.py, scripts/coord/install-git-hooks.ps1 and
#                     .github/workflows/branch-leak-scan.yml, then declined to sweep them in. Naming a
#                     stale copy is a pointer, not a fix -- and a pointer whose targets get fixed goes
#                     false itself, which this one did, in the same change that fixed them. All three
#                     now state what the setting DOES and name the command above instead of quoting an
#                     answer.
#
#                     THE CENSUS IS `git grep -n enforce_admins`, and that command is the control --
#                     not any list written here, which is the thing that just rotted. A hit asserting
#                     a VALUE is what to look at. AT LEAST TWO remain, both outside the three repaired
#                     above and both left by scope rather than by judgment: scripts/hooks/push_guard.py's
#                     module DOCSTRING states the setting with its measurement date and hangs the
#                     escape-hatch reasoning off it, and docs/CI.md quotes a dated API transcript
#                     carrying it. RUN THE CENSUS rather than trusting this sentence to have stayed
#                     complete -- an enumeration here is the liability the paragraph above describes,
#                     and this one is deliberately written as a floor. Whether either should become a
#                     pointer is unfiled.
#
# This file is not the enforcement -- the server is. It is the CHECKED-IN CLAIM that every in-repo
# statement must agree with, which is what `tests/test_required_contexts.py` asserts. When branch
# protection changes, change this file in the same PR; the test will name every prose claim that
# then needs updating.
#
# FORMAT. One context string per line, `#` starts a comment, blank lines ignored. These are the
# exact strings branch protection matches -- the JOB NAME (`name:`), not the workflow name and not
# the workflow file. Two ways that bites:
#   * The CLA context is `cla` (the job key, because cla.yml's job declares no `name:`), NOT
#     "CLA Assistant" (the workflow name). docs/CI.md claimed the latter for months.
#   * A job name containing " #" must be QUOTED in YAML or it truncates at the comment marker --
#     see .github/workflows/backlog-hygiene.yml, whose name is deliberately quoted for this reason.
#
# ADDING ONE: see the required-but-absent trap in docs/CI.md. A required check that never reports
# blocks every PR forever, so confirm the job reports on a real PR (no `paths:` filter that can skip
# it, no `if:` gated on a non-PR event) BEFORE it lands here or in branch protection.

# --- ci.yml ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# `CI gate` (ci.yml, job `ci-gate`) is a ROLL-UP, not a test. It is `if: always()` over the legs
# below and fails if any of them failed or was cancelled:
#
#   PATH-GATED or nightly -- these cannot be required directly (see below):
#     sqlserver-store, postgres-store, load-test, load-test-sqlserver, windows-service-smoke, changes
#     packaging-build   (BACKLOG #1840 -- builds every distribution and runs the release member gate
#                        over the real artifacts; path-gated on packaging config, forced on push-to-main)
#   NOT path-gated -- these RUN ON EVERY PULL REQUEST and are the two most likely to report:
#     webconsole, tooling
#
# NO COUNT IS WRITTEN HERE ON PURPOSE. This block said "EIGHT legs" until `packaging-build` made it
# nine, and a number in prose is a second claim about the `needs:` list that nothing reconciles --
# the exact drift #1300 filed, one level up from the names it fixed. The names below ARE reconciled,
# by tests/test_required_contexts.py, and that test deliberately asserts no count for the same reason.
#
# THE SECOND GROUP WAS ABSENT FROM THIS FILE UNTIL BACKLOG #1300, AND THAT IS THE FAILURE THIS FILE
# EXISTS TO PREVENT. This file's whole purpose is to be the checked-in answer to "does this check
# block a merge". A session whose `repo harness tests` or `webconsole` leg is red reads this file,
# finds no such context, and concludes it is not blocking. The correct answer was always written out
# in ci.yml's `needs:` -- but a reader who knew to go there would not have needed this file.
# `tests/test_required_contexts.py` now reconciles this comment against that `needs:` list, so the
# two cannot drift again silently.
#
# Requiring the roll-up is the only way to gate those six. They cannot be required directly: a
# path-gated job does not report on a PR that touches none of its paths, which is the
# required-but-absent trap and would wedge every such PR forever. The roll-up always reports, so it is
# safe to require -- verified on a run where all six legs SKIPPED and `CI gate` still returned success.
#
# It matters because those six cover exactly what the three `test` legs SKIP: the store suites skip
# unless a leg supplies the database. Without the roll-up required, a PR touching the SQL Server or
# Postgres store, the load path, or the Windows service could merge with those legs red and nothing on
# the merge path would notice.
#
# Removed from protection 2026-07-29 (reason unrecorded) and RESTORED 2026-07-30 after checking its
# record: 18 success / 2 failure over 20 runs, and neither failure would have blocked a PR --
#   * one was a `schedule` (nightly) run whose sqlserver load-test legs failed: not a PR context;
#   * one was a superseded re-push where every job was CANCELLED. `CI gate` fails on `cancelled` by
#     design, but branch protection gates on the LATEST head SHA, so a cancelled old run does not
#     block the current head (see ci.yml's concurrency note).
CI gate
test (ubuntu-latest, py3.14)
test (windows-2022, py3.14)
test (windows-2025, py3.14)

# --- security.yml (the TWO composite roll-ups, and nothing else from that file) --------------------
#
# THIS SECTION USED TO READ "every non-advisory job in that file", AND THAT DESCRIPTION DIED WITH THE
# 2026-09-16 PROTECTION EDIT. It is kept here as the previous claim rather than overwritten, because
# the shape it described is the one a reader still expects: for two months every hard-failing job in
# security.yml was required, and `sbom` + `trivy` were absent for the single reason that they declare
# `continue-on-error: true`. There are now THREE reasons a security.yml job is absent from this list,
# and only the first is about the job's own posture:
#
#   * `sbom`, `trivy`             -- advisory BY DESIGN; they declare `continue-on-error: true`
#                                    (`sbom` on the job, `trivy` on its scan step).
#   * `released-line-audit`       -- advisory BY PLACEMENT; schedule/dispatch-only, so it can never
#                                    report on a pull request. It still goes red on a finding.
#   * the SEVEN original scans    -- SUPERSEDED. See the block below. They hard-fail and they report
#                                    on every pull request; they simply no longer gate the merge.
#
# The seven are the new case, and they are the one a reader is most likely to get wrong, because they
# look exactly like a required job from inside the workflow file.

# THE TWO COMPOSITE ROLL-UPS -- SINCE 2026-09-16, THE ONLY security.yml CONTEXTS THAT GATE A MERGE.
# They are COMPOSITE jobs running the same seven scans in two runner slots instead of seven.
# docs/CI.md carries the reasoning and the runner-slot measurement;
# tests/test_security_composite_parity.py asserts each copied body is byte-identical to its original,
# which is what makes the consolidation safe to review -- every assertion this repository already made
# about an original step is an assertion about a string the copy shares.
#
# THE OVERLAP IS HALF OVER, AND SAYING WHICH HALF IS THE POINT. Until 2026-09-16 every scan ran twice
# and BOTH copies were required, so a finding blocked the merge twice over. Now every scan still runs
# twice -- the seven original jobs are still in the workflow -- but only the composite copy is
# required. So the runner-slot saving is still unrealised (it arrives when the seven jobs are deleted,
# consolidation step 3) while the merge-gating consolidation is already complete.
#
# THEY WERE DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM THIS FILE UNTIL 2026-09-15, AND THAT ABSENCE OUTLIVED ITS REASON
# BY ABOUT A DAY. The reason was sound while it held: recording a context here before protection
# carries it is the lie this file exists to prevent. The owner then added both to protection (step 2)
# and nothing moved the file, so the absence flipped from true to false without a single edit.
# That is the shape to watch for -- a correct note whose correctness depends on a server setting it
# cannot see. It is recorded in this file's header rather than deleted, because the next staged
# context will create the same window. It recurred on 2026-09-16 in the opposite direction, which is
# the same shape again: seven lines that were true for two months became false with no edit to them.
repo-scan (bandit, semgrep, crypto-inventory, forbidden-content)
dependency-and-secret-scan (pip-audit, npm-audit, gitleaks)

# THE SEVEN ORIGINALS ARE NO LONGER REQUIRED. THEY ARE ALSO NOT GONE, AND THE GAP BETWEEN THOSE TWO
# FACTS IS THIS ENTRY. Until 2026-09-16 this block read "THE SEVEN ORIGINALS ABOVE ARE STILL REQUIRED
# AND MUST NOT BE DELETED YET" and listed steps 3 and 4 as outstanding. Step 4 has happened. The seven
# lines are struck from the list above, and the previous text is quoted rather than dropped because
# what it was warning about is what determined the order the owner then used:
#
#     bandit (Python SAST)                             pip-audit (dependency vulnerabilities)
#     npm-audit (ide dependency vulnerabilities)        gitleaks (secret scan)
#     semgrep (project SAST rules)                      crypto-inventory (ASVS 11.1.3 discovery gate)
#     forbidden-content (customer/PHI leak guard)
#
#   4. DONE, at about 2026-09-16 18:45Z. The owner removed the seven original NAMES from branch
#      protection, fifteen contexts to eight. THIS WAS STEP 4 TAKEN BEFORE STEP 3, which is the
#      inversion the previous text asked for and the safe order of the pair.
#   3. STILL TO DO, and it is now safe in any order. A later PR deletes the seven original JOBS from
#      .github/workflows/security.yml. Nothing requires those contexts any more, so the deletion can
#      no longer wedge a pull request and needs no protection edit beside it. That PR also retires
#      the `_SUPERSEDED_SECURITY_JOBS` bucket in tests/test_security_posture.py and the nine
#      re-pointed entries' provenance notes in tests/negative_controls.toml, and this block.
#
# WHAT THE ORDERING DEFECT COST, AND WHAT IT BOUGHT. The previous text called steps 3-then-4 "a real
# defect in the plan as written", because between them the seven contexts would be required and
# unreportable -- every pull request wedged. Inverting the pair costs a window of the OPPOSITE kind:
# between step 4 and step 3 the seven jobs run, consume seven runner slots, and gate nothing. That is
# wasted compute and a misleading checks tab, and it is recoverable by a single pull request. The
# other window is a wedged repository recoverable only by the owner. Recorded because the asymmetry is
# the reason to prefer this order next time, not merely the reason it worked out this time.
#
# WHILE THAT WINDOW IS OPEN THE SEVEN ARE A POSTURE THIS FILE HAS NOT HELD BEFORE: hard-failing,
# reporting on every pull request, and deliberately not required. They are not advisory BY DESIGN
# (no `continue-on-error`) and not advisory BY PLACEMENT (no schedule-only `if:` -- they do report on
# a PR). tests/test_security_posture.py files them under `_SUPERSEDED_SECURITY_JOBS` for exactly the
# length of that window, and the claim that makes the posture safe is
# tests/test_security_composite_parity.py's: each composite's copy of a scan is byte-identical to the
# original, so the scan that stopped gating is the same string as the one that now gates.

# --- cla.yml --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
cla

# --- backlog-hygiene.yml ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PROMOTED 2026-07-29 (verified against the live API the same day). Before that it hard-failed and
# nothing waited for it, so it was decoration -- auto-merge blocks only on REQUIRED contexts. It exists
# because #60 shipped while its banner still read "PRE-RESERVED", and that stale banner was then
# repeated as fact in a merged PR; in a repo where the ledger is the only memory shared across isolated
# sessions, a stale banner makes another session rebuild work that is already merged.
#
# The quoting in backlog-hygiene.yml is load-bearing: the job name contains " #", which YAML would
# truncate at the comment marker, and the job NAME is the context string.
#
# ***THIS CONTEXT STRING NO LONGER DESCRIBES ITS JOB AT ALL, AND THE STRING STILL MUST NOT CHANGE.***
# The ledger left this repository on 2026-09-13 (BACKLOG #1250). Both of the job's checks -- the
# banner rule this string names, and the diff-scoped citation gate added under BACKLOG #1095 -- read
# files that are no longer here, so the job is now a no-op that prints why.
#
# It is kept because the string is an identifier in BRANCH PROTECTION, which is not an in-repo
# setting. Deleting the job, renaming it, or dropping a trigger makes the context never report, and a
# required context that never reports does not fail -- it WEDGES every pull request, in the queue and
# out of it. Retiring it properly means removing it from branch protection FIRST and then from this
# file, in that order, which is a deliberate act by whoever holds that setting.
#
# So the name is frozen and now inaccurate. That trade is the point: for an identifier, stability is
# worth more than accuracy, and the inaccuracy is recorded here and in the workflow's own header
# rather than repaired by an edit that would break the thing.
#
# The quoting note above still applies: the job name contains " #".
a PR that implements BACKLOG #N must update BACKLOG.md
#
# ADDING ANOTHER ONE LATER: add the context to branch protection FIRST, then add the line here and
# update the count pinned in tests/test_required_contexts.py, in the same PR. In that order, because
# this file mirrors the live server -- a line added here first is exactly the lie the file exists to
# prevent. Adding to protection is all-or-nothing: the REST endpoint 422s with `already_exists` if any
# context in the request is already required, and then adds NONE of them, so send only the missing ones.

# --- review-gate.yml -- RETIRED 2026-09-04, MECHANISM AND CONTEXT BOTH GONE ------------------------
# `a reviewer has read this` was ARMED 2026-08-31 (BACKLOG #1404) and RETIRED 2026-09-04 by the owner's
# decision. The context left branch protection first and this file followed, which is the same order
# the ADDING paragraph above prescribes; `.github/workflows/review-gate.yml` was deleted in the same
# change, so no job can report that string any more. Fourteen contexts became thirteen.
#
# WHAT THE REPOSITORY NOW HAS INSTEAD IS NOTHING, and that is the state rather than a complaint about
# it. `required_approving_review_count` is 0 and has to stay 0: every session on this machine pushes as
# ONE GitHub identity (`gh` auth lives at AppData\Roaming\GitHub CLI\hosts.yml, machine-wide rather than
# per config root), CODEOWNERS assigns every path to that same account, and GitHub refuses to let an
# author approve their own pull request -- so raising the count to 1 would wedge every pull request
# permanently instead of reviewing any of them. With approvals pinned at 0 and this context withdrawn,
# no automated control reports that a green pull request was never read. A future identity-based gate
# needs a second GitHub account whose token the reviewer session carries in GH_TOKEN.
#
# THREE MEASUREMENTS FROM THE ARMING SURVIVE THE GATE, because each is about ARMING ANY REQUIRED
# CONTEXT, not about this one. The mechanism is retired; the findings are not:
#
#   * A `pull_request` WORKFLOW REPORTS ON PULL REQUESTS OLDER THAN ITSELF. GitHub runs it from the
#     MERGE commit, not from the head. VERIFIED 2026-08-31 on PR 713: its head 5cb51e46 returned 404
#     for the workflow file and the context reported on it anyway. So arming a new required context
#     strands no open pull request, and the remedy for one is never a rebase.
#   * A REQUIRED WORKFLOW MUST DECLARE `merge_group:` OR NOTHING MERGES. A required context whose
#     workflow lacks that trigger never reports on a queue entry. Measured and recorded at its source
#     in codeql.yml's header under BACKLOG #340 -- 32 check-runs green and three contexts simply
#     absent, on the first entry the queue ever held.
#   * A CONTROL BUILT ON ONE TRIGGER CAN BE BLIND TO ITS OWN REMOVAL. Dropping `labeled` from the
#     retired workflow's `types:` list would have left a gate no reviewer action could clear: the label
#     fired no run, and the only trigger that still re-ran the job was `synchronize`, whose first step
#     REMOVED the label. Measured 2026-08-31, before a test existed for it -- dropping `labeled`
#     reddened NOTHING and 65 tests passed. That is why a trigger list is load-bearing and needs its
#     own test, which is true of every workflow here, not only the one that taught it.
#
# THE `reviewed` LABEL HAS NO CONSUMER LEFT. .github/workflows/unread-signal.yml and
# scripts/ci/check_unread_prs.py were its last readers. The owner ruled the signal off on 2026-09-08,
# the workflow was disabled on the server the same day, and both files were deleted on 2026-09-13
# (BACKLOG #1490). A `reviewed` label still sitting on an open pull request is an inert leftover:
# nothing adds it, removes it, or reads it.

# DELIBERATELY NOT REQUIRED (do not add without the owner's decision; each has a recorded reason):
#   codeql.yml, scorecard.yml  -- their SARIF upload needs `security-events: write`, which fork-PR
#                                 tokens lack, so requiring them would block every fork PR.
#                                 `CodeQL (python)` and `CodeQL (javascript-typescript)` were read as
#                                 required earlier on 2026-08-31 and are NOT required at 20:57 CDT
#                                 that day. This entry is the reason that reading is the settled one,
#                                 so do not transcribe a future sighting over it -- reinstating them
#                                 is an owner decision that has to retract the fork-PR cost first.
#                                 COUPLING, added 2026-09-07: codeql.yml's `analyze` job is guarded
#                                 with `github.event_name != 'merge_group'`, so it does NOT run in
#                                 the queue (it is analysed on the PR and on the push instead, and
#                                 the queue pass was discarded). Promoting either CodeQL context to
#                                 required therefore requires REMOVING that guard in the SAME change
#                                 -- otherwise the context never reports in the queue and NOTHING
#                                 MERGES, which is the required-but-absent trap docs/CI.md names.
#                                 scorecard.yml additionally has no `pull_request` trigger at all
#                                 (`branch_protection_rule`, `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch`; the
#                                 `push` arm was deleted for cost -- see that file's own header),
#                                 so it can never report on one -- the required-but-absent trap, on
#                                 top of the token problem.
#   zizmor.yml                 -- paths-filtered, so it does not report on most PRs.
#   quality-advisory.yml       -- advisory BY DESIGN and must never be promoted; the invariant is
#                                 pinned by tests/test_quality_advisory_invariants.py.
#   dast.yml                   -- nightly/tag/dispatch only, with no pull_request trigger, so it can
#                                 never report on a PR (required-but-absent trap). Advisory by
#                                 placement, not by continue-on-error: the job goes red on a finding.
#                                 See ADR 0155.
#   security.yml's             -- `released-line-audit (latest release's pinned runtime)` is
#   released-line-audit           schedule/dispatch only, so it can never report on a PR
#                                 (required-but-absent trap). Advisory by placement, not by
#                                 continue-on-error: it goes red on a finding, and
#                                 tests/test_security_posture.py holds that. It also could not be
#                                 actioned by a PR author -- its remedy is cutting a release on the
#                                 latest line (docs/SUPPORT-POLICY.md), not editing the branch under
#                                 review. BACKLOG #1081.
#   ingress-rate-probe.yml     -- workflow_dispatch only, so it never reports on a PR. It is also
#                                 structurally unfit to gate anything: it MEASURES a runner's ingress
#                                 service rate and exits 0 even when the reconcile fails, because a
#                                 machine too slow to keep up is the finding, not an error. See #320.
